title: Trait cross-cultural curiosity: its measurement and relation to inclusive values, inclusive behaviors, and intergroup contact
abstract: Abstract What motivates people to commit themselves to cultural inclusiveness? Building on Intergroup Emotions theory and prior research on the dispositional correlates of inclusiveness, we propose that a stable tendency to be curious about other cultures could motivate inclusiveness. We conducted two studies to develop a measure of trait cross-cultural curiosity and test this prediction. This measure proved to be reliable. As hypothesized, it was related to universalist values, open-mindedness (especially its tolerance facet), positive cross-cultural contact, and collective action intentions. It predicted these forms of cross-cultural engagement above and beyond other aspects of trait curiosity. Also consistent with predictions, it was related to appraising cross-cultural interactions as novel, complex, but also comprehensible. Finally, it mediated the effect of these cross-cultural appraisals on positive contact and activist intentions. Although causal conclusions cannot be made based on these initial studies, they nonetheless lay the groundwork for research on a potential catalyst for change.
